Rebe.et: From Middle High German rëbe, from Old High German rëba, from Proto-West Germanic *rebā.

s: a female given name from English [in turn from Biblical Hebrew], variant of Rebekka

Rebus.et: Derived from Latin rebus. Cognate with English rebus, French rébus.

s: partridge (Perdix; any bird of the genus of Galliform gamebirds known collectively as the 'true partridges') (Chiefly used in plural.)
Rebhuhn.et: From Middle High German rëphuon, from Old High German rebhuon, rebahuon, cognate to or adapted from Proto-Slavic *arębъ (“partridge”) + Huhn.

s: a female given name from Biblical Hebrew, equivalent to English Rebecca; variant form Rebecca

rebeln.et: From reiben + -eln. Compare North German rebbeln, ribbeln.

s: rebbe: an Ashkenazi Orthodox rabbi, especially in a Yiddish-speaking congregation
Rebbe.et: Borrowed from Yiddish רבי (rebe). Doublet of Rabbi and Rabbiner.
